C-HDP-1.claim: H_i is bounded (docs/doctrine/protocol_w_hdp_parameter_memory.md 'Q: ... bounded, physically sane dynamics?', stability doctrine)

classification.detail: jnp.clip to [0.1, 10.0] every step, unconditional; additionally for K_ctrl > 0 the ODE has a two-sided restoring term (analytically bounded within the band); for K_ctrl = 0 and gamma = delta = 0 the drift is one-sided and only the clamp bounds it (consistently with the rho_sweep observation H pinned near H_max)

C-HDP-1.allowed_language: H is hard-clamped to [H_min, H_max] = [0.1, 10.0] at every integration step regardless of parameters or inputs

classification.detail: every-step clip to [w_floor, w_ceiling]; with K_w_ctrl > 0 the continuous-time law additionally contracts toward wmag_baseline (analytically bounded given clamped H)

C-HDP-2.allowed_language: |w| is hard-clamped to [w_floor, w_ceiling] at every integration step; with K_w_ctrl > 0 an additional restoring term pulls |w| toward its calibrated baseline

C-HDP-3.claim: DEFAULT_HDP with K_w_ctrl = 0.0 is safe with no weight-magnitude restoration

classification.detail: per user direction, K_w_ctrl = 0.0 implies nothing about instability; the shipped-preset trials remain the verified domain (see C-HDP-5). Long-horizon drift behavior with K_w_ctrl = 0.0 is not established

C-HDP-3.allowed_language: with the default K_w_ctrl = 0.0 the weight magnitude has no active restoration; boundedness across arbitrary long horizons was not established and is guaranteed only per-step by the [w_floor, w_ceiling] clamp
